svg.title: Link memory and its three messages
svg.desc: A link is one direction between two hosts, from the host that sent the flow's first packet to the other. Each link keeps a memory of 100 numbers. Three messages update it, each only once it exists: the event at 10 milliseconds after the first packet, the 20-packet summary when the 20th packet arrives, and the flow record when the flow closes (forecasting encoder only). To read an event, the context encoder combines the event's features with the memory of both link directions and attends over the latest events of up to 20 recent peers, producing s, 100 numbers.
